\paragraph{Why not standard overestimation countermeasures?}
Double Q-learning \citep{vanhasselt2016double}, TD3 \citep{fujimoto2018td3}, and ensemble critics \citep{chen2021redq} target \emph{estimation error} in the critic's training dynamics. CIVO is upstream: the RSSM's $2.78\times$ fidelity gap biases the critic's \emph{inputs}---an ensemble would converge to the same wrong value on shared biased imagination data (measurement bias vs.\ noise). MBPO \citep{janner2019mbpo} mixes real data, but DreamerV3 trains entirely within imagination. MOReL \citep{kidambi2020morel} and COMBO \citep{yu2021combo} penalize uncertainty, but the RSSM is \emph{confidently wrong} at $\dt > 1$.

A three-level intervention hierarchy spanning 9 configurations shows that no tested intervention reliably eliminates CIVO; TCN ($\sigma{=}0.2$) is the only intervention achieving complete suppression in any configuration (2 of 4 Walker seeds), but exhibits high seed sensitivity and fails to transfer across environments. These findings are directly relevant to robotics: as world-model RL moves toward real systems with variable-rate sensing and multi-timescale control, understanding when temporal conditioning fails---and why standard countermeasures cannot fix it---is essential for safe deployment.

\paragraph{Contributions.}
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item \textbf{Failure mode identification.} We identify CIVO as specific to imagination-based actor-critic with temporal conditioning and isolate trained $\dt$-embedding $+$ multi-rate exposure as jointly necessary through factorial experiments (6/6 seeds exceed NVE threshold, 5/6 collapse across two environments).
    \item \textbf{MPC vs.\ imagination boundary.} We identify the feedback architecture as the structural factor: $\dt$-conditioning succeeds in TD-MPC2's MPC re-planning but fails under imagination-based bootstrapping, where model errors compound into biased value targets with no real-data anchor.
    \item \textbf{Gradient magnitude $\neq$ causal importance.} The reward head contributes the largest gradient share (38--49\%) yet reward-only stopping fails; the observation decoder (16--22\%) is causally critical. Obs-decoder SGS achieves only 1/6 prevention, confirming redundant gradient pathways.
    \item \textbf{Three-level intervention hierarchy.} Across 9 configurations at gradient, output, and representation levels, no intervention reliably eliminates CIVO. TCN ($\sigma{=}0.2$) is the only intervention achieving complete suppression (2 of 4 Walker seeds) but exhibits high seed sensitivity and 0\% cross-environment transfer, positioning it as a diagnostic probe for the representation level rather than a deployable mitigation.
    \item \textbf{Online detection.} A lightweight NVE-based detector achieves 100\% sensitivity (5/5) with predictive warning in 2/5 cases, enabling early termination of compromised runs.
\end{enumerate}

tool_args.content: Temporal abstraction via variable-rate imagination promises to extend the effective planning horizon of world-model reinforcement learning, and $\Delta t$-conditioning has proven effective in model-predictive control (MPC) methods. We find that this approach cannot be directly transferred to imagination-based actor-critic training: every variable-rate configuration of DreamerV3 we test degrades performance to 14--30\% of baseline. Through factorial diagnostics on two continuous-control tasks, we identify the combination of trained temporal embedding and multi-rate data exposure as the causal factor and characterize the resulting failure mode: \emph{conditioning-induced value overestimation} (CIVO). The trained embedding enables the RSSM reward head to develop a $2.78\times$ prediction gap between $\Delta t{=}1$ and $\Delta t{=}2$, which the critic internalizes as optimistic values ($n{=}6$ seeds, two environments, AUROC${=}0.971$). The contrast with MPC methods identifies the feedback architecture (imagination-based bootstrapping versus re-planning) as the structural factor. A four-level intervention hierarchy spanning gradient, output, representation, and architecture levels reveals that no tested intervention reliably eliminates CIVO across environments. Gradient magnitude does not predict causal importance: the reward head contributes the largest gradient share (38--49\%) yet reward-only stopping fails. In pure-imagination training, dual critics converge to identical value functions ($\rho > 0.999$), rendering Double Q pessimism ineffective; the min operation nonetheless enables CIVO recovery, while prevention requires min $+$ increased capacity. A lightweight online detector identifies all CIVO cases (100\% sensitivity) with predictive warning in 2/5 cases.

707	\subsection{Cross-Simulator Specificity (PickCube)}
708	
709	Exp\_019b applies the CIVO-trigger configuration to PickCube-v1 in ManiSkill3, a manipulation task with sparse rewards. The V/E ratio exhibits an oscillatory pattern rather than monotonic divergence: it spikes to $r_t = 5.66$ at 52.5K, then deflates to 1.38 by 72.5K. This trajectory prevents the acceleration condition from co-occurring with evaluation decline at any single checkpoint. Across all 14 checkpoints through 132.5K, the detector correctly remains silent (TN), confirming that the acceleration filter distinguishes transient spikes from CIVO's sustained monotonic divergence.

711	\subsection{Detector Limitations}
712	
713	Four constraints bound the current detector. First, the three-checkpoint window cannot distinguish transient dips from sustained collapse. Second, the acceleration condition assumes monotonically increasing overestimation during onset. Third, the detector identifies a \emph{pattern} rather than a \emph{mechanism}: run 009c shows that non-CIVO pathologies produce the same signature. Fourth, threshold values were calibrated on fourteen runs across three environments; generalization to different reward scales requires further validation.

We test whether critic capacity and Double Q pessimism \citep{fujimoto2018td3} address CIVO (\S\ref{sec:dual_critic_method}; Table~\ref{tab:intervention_hierarchy}). Across all dual-critic configurations ($n{=}7$, three environments), the two critics converge to near-identical value functions ($\rho > 0.999$), with per-sample pessimism at 3--4\% of the independent-critic bound. Both critics train on shared RSSM features with no real-data anchor, eliminating the representational diversity underlying Double Q's effectiveness in model-free RL.

\paragraph{Recovery (min-dominated).} The min operation enables robust CIVO recovery without preventing onset. Narrow dual-critic experiences CIVO in both seeds (exp\_035: $\nve = 2.75\times$, eval $33.8 \to 697.8$; exp\_039: $\nve = 2.19\times$, eval $35.9 \to 592.7$), with full recovery in both (recovery ratio ${\sim}16$--$19\times$). This outperforms wide single-critic (exp\_033, eval 407.9) despite $2\times$ fewer parameters, isolating the min operation as the dominant recovery factor.

\paragraph{Prevention (min $+$ capacity).} CIVO prevention requires the min operation and increased capacity acting together: only wide dual-critic (exp\_032, 3 seeds) maintains $\nve \leq 1.4\times$ throughout (3/3 CIVO prevention). However, prevention does not guarantee stability: 1/3 seeds (exp\_038) avoids CIVO ($\nve \leq 0.3\times$) yet collapses via a mechanistically distinct non-CIVO pathway (eval $354 \to 120.9$, actor entropy increase from $-3.59$ to $-0.45$), yielding 2/3 performance stability. Cross-environment transfer is limited: on Cheetah, wide dual-critic reduces NVE from $8.27\times$ to $1.75\times$ but does not prevent onset (Appendix~\ref{sec:dual_critic_appendix}).

We test whether critic capacity and Double Q pessimism \citep{fujimoto2018td3} address CIVO (\S\ref{sec:dual_critic_method}; Table~\ref{tab:intervention_hierarchy}). Across all dual-critic configurations ($n{=}7$, three environments), the two critics converge to near-identical value functions ($\rho > 0.999$), with per-sample pessimism at 3--4\% of the independent-critic bound. Both critics train on shared RSSM features with no real-data anchor, eliminating the representational diversity underlying Double Q's effectiveness in model-free RL.

\paragraph{Recovery (min-dominated).} The min operation enables robust CIVO recovery without preventing onset. Narrow dual-critic experiences CIVO in both seeds (exp\_035: $\nve = 2.75\times$, eval $33.8 \to 697.8$; exp\_039: $\nve = 2.19\times$, eval $35.9 \to 592.7$), with full recovery in both (recovery ratio ${\sim}16$--$19\times$). This outperforms wide single-critic (exp\_033, eval 407.9) despite $2\times$ fewer parameters, isolating the min operation as the dominant recovery factor.

\paragraph{Prevention (min $+$ capacity).} CIVO prevention requires the min operation and increased capacity acting together: only wide dual-critic (exp\_032, 3 seeds) maintains $\nve \leq 1.4\times$ throughout (3/3 CIVO prevention). However, prevention does not guarantee stability: 1/3 seeds (exp\_038) avoids CIVO ($\nve \leq 0.3\times$) yet collapses via a mechanistically distinct non-CIVO pathway (eval $354 \to 120.9$, actor entropy increase from $-3.59$ to $-0.45$), yielding 2/3 performance stability. Cross-environment transfer is limited: on Cheetah, wide dual-critic reduces NVE from $8.27\times$ to $1.75\times$ but does not prevent onset (Appendix~\ref{sec:dual_critic_appendix}).
